business.hours: The phone line is answered 24 hours a day, 7 days a week by an automated assistant.
business.description: A free phone line for pool cleaning, pool repair and pool service across the Phoenix metro. An automated assistant answers 24/7 and transfers callers to an independent, locally owned pool service company.
business.short_disclosure: Phoenix Pool Cleaning Pro is a free phone line, not a pool company. It answers your call and connects you with an independent local pool service company, which inspects, quotes and does the work, and which you pay directly.
business.referral_disclosure: Companies may pay a referral fee. You never pay the line.

areas.name: North Phoenix
areas.summary: The northern City of Phoenix villages, from North Mountain to North Gateway, on hard city water and City of Phoenix pool rules.

areas.name: Scottsdale
areas.summary: Scottsdale Water delivers mostly CAP and SRP surface water, with hardness from 16 grains per gallon north to 25 in the south.

areas.name: Paradise Valley
areas.summary: Town incorporated in 1961 around one acre lots, served by several water companies, with many homes on septic below Camelback and Mummy Mountain.

areas.name: Fountain Hills
areas.summary: Planned town founded in 1970 on hillsides below the McDowell Mountains, with very hard EPCOR water and strict rules keeping pool water on the lot.

areas.name: Cave Creek
areas.summary: A desert foothills town that runs its own water utility on Central Arizona Project water piped from the canal.

areas.name: Carefree
areas.summary: A small desert town whose water company delivers CAP water treated under agreements with Scottsdale and Cave Creek.

areas.name: Anthem
areas.summary: An unincorporated master-planned community on Interstate 17 whose EPCOR water reports about 18 grains per gallon of hardness.

areas.name: Tempe
areas.summary: Tempe draws about 87 percent of its water from the Salt and Verde rivers, and requires five foot pool fences by city code.

areas.name: Mesa
areas.summary: Mesa sorts tap water hardness by zone, about 12 to 16 grains on average, and wants pools drained to the sewer cleanout.

areas.name: Chandler
areas.summary: Chandler blends Salt, Verde and Colorado River water with groundwater, averaging 16.5 grains of hardness, and grew from 30,000 people in 1980.

areas.name: Gilbert
areas.summary: Incorporated in 1920 and still a town, with water that blends SRP and CAP supplies averaging 8 to 10 grains of hardness.

areas.name: Ahwatukee
areas.summary: A City of Phoenix urban village south of South Mountain, first built in the 1970s and annexed by 1987.

areas.name: Queen Creek
areas.summary: A fast-growing former farm town in Maricopa and Pinal counties, incorporated in 1989, on well water of 6 to 17 grains.

areas.name: San Tan Valley
areas.summary: A Pinal County community of over 100,000 that voted in 2025 to become a town on July 1, 2026.

areas.name: Apache Junction
areas.summary: Straddles Maricopa and Pinal counties below the Superstition Mountains, with two hard water providers, SRP power and many winter residents.

areas.name: Maricopa
areas.summary: A young Pinal County city, incorporated in 2003, that grew from about 1,000 residents to roughly 73,300.

areas.name: Glendale
areas.summary: West Valley city whose tap water blends Salt and Verde river water, Colorado River water through CAP, and city wells.

areas.name: Peoria
areas.summary: Long West Valley city that shares Colorado River water and the Pyramid Peak treatment plant with Glendale for its northern neighborhoods.

areas.name: Surprise
areas.summary: Surprise runs its own water utility while EPCOR serves some addresses, and city rules keep drained pool water off streets.

areas.name: Sun City
areas.summary: Community served by EPCOR water, where this page covers private backyard pools rather than the recreation center pools.

areas.name: Litchfield Park
areas.summary: Founded in 1916 as a Goodyear cotton town, with hard Liberty Utilities well water and streets of palms and orange trees.

areas.name: Goodyear
areas.summary: Grew from 65,275 to 95,294 residents in the decade to 2020, with Interstate 10 splitting water service between the city and Liberty Utilities.

areas.name: Avondale
areas.summary: Avondale blends Colorado River water delivered through Phoenix with city well water, so mineral levels at the tap can shift.

areas.name: Buckeye
areas.summary: Buckeye's city water comes only from wells in the Hassayampa sub-basin, and three different providers serve parts of the city.

areas.name: Laveen
areas.summary: Former farm and dairy country between South Mountain and the Salt River, partly a Phoenix village and partly unincorporated county.
